title: Nonconvex stationarity with priced value-gradient and full-Hessian jets under joint smoothness
summary: A high-dimensional weighted oracle frontier connects a mixed-query rate with the gradient-only accuracy exponent.

description_paragraphs: Find an approximate first-order stationary point while minimizing the weighted number of ordinary value-gradient and rich full-Hessian queries.
task.formulation: Find an approximate first-order stationary point while minimizing the weighted number of ordinary value-gradient and rich full-Hessian queries.

description_paragraphs: The unknown bounded-below $C^2$ objective $f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ satisfies $f(0)-\inf f\le1$, $\operatorname{Lip}(\nabla f)\le1$ and $\operatorname{Lip}(\nabla^2f)\le1$, with Euclidean operator norms. These are fixed normalized budgets; no convexity or bounded query domain is imposed.

references.title: Matching Gradient--Hessian Query Bounds via a Smooth Macro-Block Construction
references.contribution_note: An alternative globally smooth macro-block construction and proof for the matching weighted gradient–Hessian query rate. The manuscript acknowledges that the same weighted rate follows from the existing hierarchical tradeoff construction, and emphasizes its globally C-infinity realization, delayed-disclosure argument, and explicit analytic and oracle accounting. The upper-bound algorithms are drawn from prior work.

relations.description: The information packets agree, but this model adds a gradient-Lipschitz bound and a public weighted cost.
The neighboring strict-cap derivative-only problem does not bundle gradients with Hessians.
